name: LA VORO Iidabashi (LA VORO 飯田橋店 / ラ ボーロ)

claims.text: Entire product line is 100% rice flour with no wheat products made at the shop, greatly reducing cross-contact risk; however a fully dedicated wheat-free-facility statement was not verified, so confirm the workshop uses no wheat.
Not applicable — sweets-only shop; no soy sauce or savory items.
All items contain egg and milk (allergen listing 卵・米粉・乳); no vegan production.
Shop markets to wheat-allergic customers: 「小麦アレルギーの方でも安心して召し上がれます」; each product's allergen (卵・米粉・乳, モンコーネ also アーモンド) is listed on the online store.
100% 米粉 gluten-free baumkuchen specialist using own-farm raw rice flour; venue states 「グルテンフリーのため安心してお召し上がりいただけます」.
Press confirms 「米粉100％のグルテンフリーバウムクーヘン」 with per-item allergen labeling.

name: オタコ（シフォンケーキの店 otaco） (otaco (Otako) — Chiffon Cake Shop otaco)

claims.text: No wheat flour is kept anywhere on the premises, and no baking powder is used in the chiffon cakes — the batter is a 100% rice-flour base leavened only by whipped egg foam.
Highlighted by gluten-free-focused bloggers as a reassuring option for people with wheat allergies because the entire kitchen is flour-free rather than just offering a token gluten-free item.

name: RICE HACK Gluten-free Bakery（ライスハック グルテンフリーベーカリー） (RICE HACK Gluten-free Bakery)

claims.text: RICE HACK is a bakery dedicated to 100% gluten-free rice-flour products; no wheat flour is used in its breads, which were developed specifically so people with celiac disease or wheat allergy can eat safely.
Reviewers on international gluten-free travel platforms describe it as a must-visit bakery in Tokyo for people with celiac disease, highlighting the rice-flour baguette and a vegan marinara pizza.
Listed as a dedicated gluten-free bakery on multiple English-language celiac/gluten-free directories.
The cafe describes its kitchen as completely gluten-free, with no wheat brought into the kitchen at all — every menu item is gluten-free by design rather than by substitution.
The cafe is 100% plant-based across its entire menu and holds vegan certification from NPO Vege Project Japan, with no animal-derived ingredients (including dairy, egg, honey) used anywhere.
Because every dish on the menu is both vegan and gluten-free, diners don't need to cross-check individual items for hidden animal or wheat ingredients.
The owner built the cafe specifically around natural, additive-free vegan cooking, using carefully selected organic and domestic ingredients.

name: ametuchi COFFEE & ORGANIC BAKED (アメツチ コーヒー＆オーガニックベイクド)

claims.text: 自家製ライ麦パンは有機小麦『春よ恋』＋有機ライ麦＋天然酵母で焼いており、店内キッチンで小麦粉を扱う=共用調理環境。
卵・チーズ・バターを使うトーストやケーキが主力で、乳・卵と同一環境。
『小麦アレルギーの人も楽しめるメニューを』と掲げ、米粉ワッフル・米粉キャロットケーキをグルテンフリーとして提供。
特別栽培米の米粉と有機米油を使った米粉キャロットケーキをグルテンフリーとして明示。
No dedicated GF preparation zone or cross-contamination protocols have been documented in any published source. The kitchen is a compact solo-operated space; separation cannot be assumed.
No source confirms whether wheat-free tamari or GF soy sauce is used. Standard Japanese soy sauce contains wheat; celiacs should ask explicitly before ordering.
All menu items are stated to be 100% plant-based; no animal products are used in the kitchen, so vegan cross-contact risk appears negligible based on the café's stated concept.

The owner is allergy-aware and deliberately excludes almond powder from sweets; she also accommodates gokunin-nuki (five-pungent-free) requests. However, formal allergen-handling procedures are not documented.
Entire menu is 100% plant-based — no fish, meat, dairy, or eggs used anywhere in the kitchen, eliminating the main vegan cross-contact vectors.
Sweets are made with rice flour and okara instead of wheat flour, meaning several dessert items are naturally gluten-free in their base formulation.
English menu available; owner is communicative with foreign guests, making dietary questions easier to raise.

name: カフェ&レンタルスペース カリカリちゃん (Cafe & Rental Space Karikari-chan)

claims.text: No dedicated GF kitchen or formal cross-contamination protocol has been confirmed. The café is a small space handling both wheat-free snacks and daily-changing lunch menus that may include wheat-based ingredients. Celiac diners should exercise caution.

No explicit information found on whether wheat-based soy sauce (醤油) is used in the lunch cooking. Standard Japanese soy sauce contains wheat; macrobiotic kitchens sometimes use tamari but this has not been confirmed here.

The lunch menu changes daily and animal products (dairy, egg, fish) occasionally appear in dishes. On vegan-style days the menu is fully plant-based, but cross-contact from shared equipment on other days is unconfirmed.
Staff are described as willing to address food allergy and vegetarian preferences upon request, but no formal allergen management system or written allergen menu has been confirmed.
All food and sweets are additive-free (無添加) since the business began — no artificial preservatives, colorings, or flavor enhancers.
The signature snacks — brown rice flour (玄米粉) mini muffins and okara-oat cookie sandwiches — are made without wheat flour and are explicitly gluten-free by ingredient.
Lunch frequently uses organic vegetables from the local Himeji Yuuki Yasai no Kai (姫路有機野菜の会) cooperative, with simple seasoning to let ingredients shine.

Venue explicitly markets its counter baked goods and bread as "allグルテンフリー," but it is not a dedicated gluten-free kitchen: the same premises also prepares the omakase lunch, which can contain wheat (seitan-type vegan proteins and a wheat white bread), so shared-surface cross-contact for the lunch is plausible and unconfirmed.
No published statement on whether soy sauce used in the vegan lunch is wheat-based shoyu or tamari; standard Japanese soy sauce contains wheat, so this must be asked when reserving.
Fully vegan kitchen (完全菜食) — no animal products used anywhere, so vegan cross-contact is not a concern.

Owners are vegan and run an additive-free, allergen-conscious bakery (egg/dairy/white-sugar-free, gluten-free), suggesting willingness to discuss diet, but no specific celiac/gluten-allergy protocol is documented; the reservation-only, one-group-per-day lunch format allows dish-by-dish confirmation in advance by phone.
Retail baked goods and bread are the venue's own declared "allグルテンフリー" line — a reliable GF choice for a celiac.
Fully vegan, completely additive-free kitchen using ~50 seasonal pesticide-free vegetables; small one-group-per-day format enables personalized advance requests.
